findings.summary: New text "Commit the session's other edits first." gives unattended session end a second commit of unspecified session edits (status --fix repairs, knowledge rows, decision-log answers, possibly entry files). The reason is real: tidy --verify refuses any untracked file (cleanup.mjs:683) and any changed file no fixable finding names (cleanup.mjs:701), so with a dirty tree verify can never pass. But brief decision end-commit = "one" says "the agent commits once", and its context says "Today approval to edit is not approval to commit" and "This extends a standing rule"; the cleanup skill still says approval to edit is not approval to commit (SKILL.md:47-48). Reading A (session end makes only the one printed commit) fails this criterion; reading B (the one printed tidy commit, other commits out of scope) passes it. Owner options: allow the pre-commit; or skip tidy and report when the tree holds other edits; or tell the agent to leave unrelated edits for the user and run tidy only on a clean tree. The skill also does not say what to do when the user's own unrelated edits are in the tree.

Spec 12 (17eba35) replaced "it never edits." with "Session end edits only the lines that `cleanup.mjs tidy` names." That is false against surviving rules: in its session-end mode the cleanup skill replaces Joycraft's managed block in AGENTS.md and re-points a dead path with one Git rename (joycraft-cleanup SKILL.md:26-31, run right after tidy by session-end SKILL.md:50), and update.md:33 calls the block replacement the one unattended entry-file edit. The cleanup skill tells the agent to read this reference first, so the agent gets two opposite rules for the same run. Fix: limit the sentence to the tidy step, or name the managed-block and rename fixes (no new words needed beyond a few).
